detail.longDescription: In Pymunk, I can call the .remove() method of a Space to remove bodies, shapes and/or constraints from it. However, it will raise an error if the object doesn't exist in the space (e.g. was already removed). Example: import pymunk space = pymunk.Space() body = pymunk.Body() space.add(body) space.remove(body) space.remove(body) # call it again On the second .remove() call, I get: Traceback (most recent call last): File "c:\Users\CHU0094\Downloads\x\main.py", line 7, in <module> space.remove(body) File "C:\Program Files\Python310\lib\site-packages\pymunk\space.py", line 401, in remove self._remove(*objs) File "C:\Program Files\Python310\lib\site-packages\pymunk\space.py", line 413, in _remove self._remove_body(o) File "C:\Program Files\Python310\lib\site-packages\pymunk\space.py", line 470, in _remove_body assert body in self._bodies, "body not in space, already removed?" AssertionError: body not in space, already removed? How can I remove object(s) from a space only if they are present? E.g. a space.discard(*objs) method? (Similar to set.remove() vs set.discard() , and list.remove() vs list.discard() .)
